rawFindings.title: Incorrect Class Name String Comparison for HashMap in V1 Encoder
rawFindings.explanation: In the v1 encoder's writeObject method, the code changed from comparing obj.$class against both javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.map ('java.util.Map') and javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.iMap (likely 'java.util.HashMap') to only against javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.map. This means that if obj.$class is 'java.util.HashMap', it will no longer reset className to an empty string and will instead keep the original class name. This is a regression from the previous behavior which treated both Map and HashMap
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the original condition to cover both 'java.util.Map' and 'java.util.HashMap' class names, e.g., keep the check: obj.$class === javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.map || obj.$class === javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.iMap, to preserve the prior encoding semantics for HashMap.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect class name comparison for java.util.HashMap in v1 encoder
rawFindings.explanation: The code compares obj.$class to javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.map and then always assigns className to such or obj.$class. The original code also compared obj.$class === javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.iMap but this was removed. If javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.iMap differs from DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.map, this change can cause mismatches for 'java.util.Map' class names and lead to incorrect omission of the className during encoding, potentially producing wrong encoded data.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the original comparison to include both DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.map and DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.iMap for correct detection.
